description:
You are an equity analyst at the Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC). The agency must fulfill a state mandate to identify zones in San Francisco where low-income residents have the worst access to employment — a condition the state defines as an 'equity transportation gap'. Zones qualifying as equity gaps are eligible for dedicated transit funding under SB 375.

Using the San Francisco UrbanSim dataset at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/data/sanfran_public.h5, compute an Equity Gap Score for every zone that has at least one household. The score must jointly reflect how income-constrained a zone's residents are AND how few jobs are locally accessible. How you define 'locally accessible' — whether that is jobs in the zone itself, jobs in a radius of zones, or any other spatial definition — is your methodological decision. However, your score must increase when a zone has more low-income households and fewer nearby jobs.

For this analysis:
- Define 'low-income' as households with income below the 30th percentile of all SF households
- Use the jobs table (sector_id and building_id columns) linked through buildings and parcels to assign jobs to zones
- Compute your equity gap score at the zone level and normalize it to [0, 1]

Deliver:
- /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/zone_accessibility.csv — one row per zone with columns: zone_id, total_jobs, total_households, low_income_households, low_income_share, jobs_per_household, equity_gap_score
- /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/equity_gap_chart.png — horizontal bar chart of the 15 zones with the highest equity_gap_score (i.e., worst equity), sorted descending, with zone_id labels on y-axis

The analysis must run in /home/ga/urbansim_projects/notebooks/job_accessibility_equity.ipynb using the UrbanSim (Python 3) kernel. Jupyter Lab is open at http://localhost:8888.
